stances.claim: The 15 justices were unanimous in being magnanimous to the seniors (upholding the 20% discount), but divided on who shoulders the cost -- del Castillo's majority allowed sellers to bear 68% via tax deduction and government 32% via foregone corporate income tax, justified by police power to regulate liberty/property for public welfare not unreasonable, oppressive or confiscatory, with sellers free to recoup via non-senior price increases.

Carpio's vigorous dissent argues government should shoulder the full cost: the discount is not a voluntary sales discount but state forcibly taking part of the purchase price from private sellers without just compensation -- under eminent domain private property cannot be taken without just compensation, so RA 9257 should be declared unconstitutional and RA 7492 (the original tax-credit framework) should be revived.
stances.confidence: stated as Carpio's position (CJP signals follow-up rather than endorsing or rejecting)

stances.claim: The case is important not only for upholding the discount but for disclosing the justices' philosophical and sociological mindset on the role of law in economics, finance, and business -- the case deserves another column on the magistrates' views vis-à-vis Panganiban's own legal philosophy of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law.

On legal and humanitarian grounds, the Sandiganbayan's order allowing GMA family visits at Veterans Memorial Medical Center for Christmas and New Year's Day deserves agreement -- three justifications: presumption of innocence (no conviction), pending bail petition (evidence not yet ruled strong), frail health (three life-threatening surgeries, metal-brace spine subject to slippage), with minimal escape risk and short-duration visits, in the spirit of peace and reconciliation commemorating the birth of the Lord of Peace.

notable_anecdotes: The 68%/32% cost-allocation arithmetic -- sellers bear 68% via tax deduction (vs full tax credit), government bears 32% via foregone corporate income tax -- the column's central technical insight stripped of legalese.

Carpio's eminent-domain reframing as 'forcibly taking part of the purchase price from private sellers without just compensation' -- a sharp doctrinal reconceptualization of what looks like a regulatory measure.

The seller-recoupment reasoning -- 'nothing prevents the sellers from recouping their subsidies to seniors by increasing their prices for the nonseniors' -- the Court's most pragmatic-economic justification, captured as a passing aside but revealing.

The four-justice opinion roster (del Castillo majority + Velasco concurrence + Bersamin concurrence + Leonen concurring-and-dissenting + Carpio dissent) compressed into a single paragraph as a glimpse of internal Court divisions.

The Spirit-of-Christmas postscript -- applying CJP's three-justification humanitarian framework (presumption of innocence + pending bail + frail health) to defend GMA's holiday family visits in the spirit of the Lord of Peace -- a striking CJP move toward a politically polarizing detainee within a column about senior-citizen discounts.

GMA medical detail -- 'Medically, she is not over the hump, as the metal brace surgically installed on her spine could slip at any time and may result in severe nerve injury, if not death' -- clinical precision rare in CJP's columns.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban reports the Supreme Court's Manila Memorial Park v. DSWD (Dec 3 2013, J. Mariano C. del Castillo ponente) decision affirming the constitutionality and mandatory character of the 20-percent senior-citizen discount on a broad range of purchases (hotels, restaurants, recreation centers, medicine, funeral and burial services, theaters, cinema houses, concert halls, circuses, carnivals, medical and dental services). The 15 justices were unanimous on the discount but divided on cost-bearing. He traces the legislative evolution: under the original RA 7492 (April 23 1992), the government bore the full discount via tax credit; at BIR initiative RA 9257 (Feb 26 2004) treated it as a tax deduction, leaving sellers to bear 68 percent and the government 32 percent (foregone corporate income tax). The majority justified this with police power to regulate liberty/property for public welfare provided not unreasonable, oppressive or confiscatory, noting that nothing prevents sellers from recouping their subsidies by increasing non-senior prices. The 38-page del Castillo ponencia drew lively concurring opinions from Velasco and Bersamin, a novel concurring-and-dissenting opinion from Leonen, and a vigorous dissent from Senior Justice Antonio T. Carpio, who argued the government should shoulder the full cost: the discount is not voluntary but state forcibly taking part of the purchase price from private sellers without just compensation -- under eminent domain, private property cannot be taken without just compensation, so RA 9257 should be declared unconstitutional and the original RA 7492 tax-credit framework should be revived. Panganiban flags that the case is important not only for upholding the discount but for disclosing the justices' philosophical and sociological mindset on the role of law in economics, finance, and business -- deserving another column on those views vis-à-vis his own legal philosophy of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law. He appends a Spirit-of-Christmas postscript agreeing on legal and humanitarian grounds with the Sandiganbayan's order allowing former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo's family to visit and stay with her at the Veterans Memorial Medical Center on Christmas and New Year's Day. Three justifications: she has not been convicted (constitutional presumption of innocence still applies); her bail petition is still pending (evidence has not been ruled strong); and she suffers from frail health (three life-threatening surgeries, metal brace surgically installed on her spine that could slip at any time causing severe nerve injury or death) plus mental stress, with minimal escape risk and short-duration well-guarded visits. In the spirit of peace and reconciliation commemorating the birth of the Lord of Peace, he believes President Arroyo deserves to enjoy the love and comfort of her family.
